ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the middle of the attached figure is a regular hexagon, completely surrounded by a ring of figures; it can be seen that outside each side of the regular hexagon there is a square attached, and between adjacent squares there is an equilateral-triangle wedge-shaped region. The outer outline is composed of the sides of these outside figures, not of the sides of the middle hexagon. Reasoning: The problem gives that the side length of the regular hexagon is 1. Each square is attached along one side of the regular hexagon, so the side length of the square is also 1. The equilateral triangles between adjacent squares share sides with the squares, so the side length of the equilateral triangles is also 1. Count the exposed sides along the outer boundary: 6 squares each contribute 1 outer side, and 6 equilateral triangles each contribute 1 outer side, for a total of 12 outer sides. Each has length 1, so the perimeter is 12 × 1 = 12.

method.method_draft: Trace only the exposed outer boundary in the image. Read from the image that the central hexagon is completely surrounded: each hexagon side has a square attached, and between adjacent squares there is one equilateral triangular wedge. The outside contour is made of 12 exposed unit-length sides: one outside side from each of the 6 squares and one outside side from each of the 6 triangles. Use the text fact that the regular hexagon has side length 1; since the squares attach along hexagon sides, square sides are length 1, and the equilateral triangles share sides with those squares, so their sides are also length 1. Therefore the perimeter is 12 exposed sides times 1, giving 12.

method.method_draft: Compute by adding the perimeters of all individual pieces and subtracting internal shared edges. From the text and image, there is one regular hexagon, six squares, and six equilateral triangles. The hexagon has perimeter 6, the six squares contribute 6·4=24, and the six equilateral triangles contribute 6·3=18, all in unit side lengths. Total separate perimeter is 48. From the image, the internal glued edges are: 6 edges where the squares attach to the hexagon, plus 12 edges where each triangle attaches to two neighboring squares, for 18 internal unit edges. Each internal edge was counted twice in the separate-perimeter total, so subtract 2·18=36. The tessellation perimeter is 48−36=12.
